card.problem: The live bot (h0, a trend follower) loses on average about -276 pts per session after a day whose range is in the top quartile, against about 0 on other days. Its losing days are choppy ones, where the open-to-close move is a small share of the high-to-low range. The early-session trend after a wide day does not follow through.
card.motivation: The reference bot's losses point at whoever is on the other side: on the day after a wide range, fading the move since the open from 11:00 earned about +9bp a session for prior range above 1.3 ATR (n=111, t about 2.0, non-negative in every year 2022-2026; my scan, not a result). That is the regime where trend bets keep losing. It differs from h5 (a 60-bar z-score fade on any day) and h6 (a break of the previous day's range): it is a once-a-day fade gated by how wide yesterday was.
card.approach: On sessions after a wide-range day, at 11:00 fade the direction of the move since the open and hold to 15:15, with a take-profit cap.
card.plan: Features ph = prev_day(high), pl = prev_day(low), a = atr(days 14), r = ret_since(anchor session_open), m = minute_of_day. Entry at m == 105 (11:00): short if r > 0 and (ph - pl) / a > p.w, long if r < 0 and (ph - pl) / a > p.w, max_per_day 1. Exit take_atr 1.0, stop_atr 1.0, time 15:15. CPCV over w in [1.05, 1.3].
card.mechanism: After a wide-range day, breakout and trend-following traders (the live bot among them) enter early in the direction of the move, expecting volatility to carry on. The informed part of the move is done the day before, so their flow overshoots and the late morning reverts as liquidity providers, and option writers rebalancing deltas around strikes after the vol spike, take the other side. The trend traders keep paying because their rules ignore yesterday's range, as the live bot's -276 pts/day in this quartile shows.
card.rule: at minute_of_day == 105, if (prev_day high - prev_day low) / atr > p.w: short if ret_since open > 0, long if < 0; exit take 1 ATR, stop 1 ATR, or 15:15

w.source: Top-quartile cutoff of the prior-day range / 14-day ATR over 2022-2026 (0.75 quantile = 1.05), the quartile where the live bot loses -276 pts/day. 1.3 is the 0.9 quantile, in the grid.

kill: the same fade on days with prior range below the median does as well (ablation of the wide clause), which would mean it is not about yesterday's range
best 5 days carry >= 50% of net (my uncapped scan had 0.63)

cpcv.note: N=12 k=2 11 paths, 100% positive, SR sd 0.00

synthetic_exit.note: AR(1) phi=1.0000; exit beats 78% of 400 synthetic exits

At the 11:00 bar, when yesterday's high-low range divided by the 14-day ATR is above w, it fades the move since the open: short if that move is up, long if it is down. It trades at most once a day and exits on a 1 ATR take, a 1 ATR stop or at 15:15. w is 1.05. The card gives only two grid values, 1.05 and 1.3, and the schema needs three centred on 1.05, so I added 0.8 as the low point. The card doesn't source 0.8. Sizing follows the reference spec, since the card gives none. It passes the spec loader.

- passed: probe (clean), determinism (identical), min_bets (201 vs ≥50), cpcv (0.63 vs >0.0, positive-path share ≥0.8), ablation (3/3 clauses hurt when removed, so every clause is earning its place), synthetic_exit (0.79 vs ≥0.5, a flag check).

- patch: patch 1 of 4 was allowed, so it isn't a hard stop. The negative gross says the signal itself loses before costs, so cutting costs won't fix it.
